Criterion: Verify that each electrically powered fire protection subsystem (e.g., fire detection, extinguishing, and explosion suppression) is provided power at all times during air vehicle operations, including electrical power system failure conditions, engine start and battery operations. Standard: Power is provided to all fire protection equipment during all phases of operation, including electrical power system failure conditions, engine start and battery operations. Method of Compliance: Analysis demonstrates that electrical power is provided to the fire protection system under all phases of operation, including electrical power system failure conditions, engine start and battery operations. Component laboratory tests and simulation tests verify the ability of the fire protection system to operate at all times including electrical power failure conditions. Ground and flight tests verify the ability of the fire protection system to operate at all flight and ground conditions including electrical power system failure conditions. References: JSSG-2009: G.3.4.7.20, G.4.4.7.20; G.3.4.7.21, G.4.4.7.21 MIL-HDBK-221: 2.7.4 14 CFR 23.851-23.865, 25.851-25.869, 23.1181-23.1203, 25.1181-25.1207, 23.1411, 25.1411, 27.863, 27.865, 29.851, 29.863, 29.865, 27.1411, 29.1411

Standard: Electrical power is provided to all electrically powered fire protection equipment (e.g., fire detection, isolation, suppression) during all phases of operation, including EPS failure conditions, engine start, and battery operations. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Conduct inspection of electrical design documentation that shows electrical power is provided to all electrically powered fire protection equipment during all phases of operation, including power failure conditions, engine start, and battery operations. Analysis.
  (1) Conduct analysis that shows required electrical power is provided to all electrically powered fire protection equipment during all phases of operation, including power failure conditions, engine start, and battery operations. Test.
    (1) Lab test: Conduct lab test that shows required electrical power is provided to all electrically powered fire protection equipment during all phases of operation, including power failure conditions, engine start, and battery operations.
    (2) Ground test: Conduct ground test that shows that required electrical power is provided to all electrically powered fire protection equipment during all ground conditions and operations, including power failure conditions, engine start, and battery operations. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
    (3) Flight test: Conduct flight test that shows required electrical power is provided to all electrically powered fire protection equipment during all flight conditions and operations, including power failure conditions, engine start, and battery operations.
